names.note: Sydney Barani (City of Sydney) uses Gadigal and Gadi(gal). No official nation site given; acceptable.
Matches the corporation's own name, Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation.
ORIC page (Wayback capture; live page bot-blocked) consistently spells Yolŋu with eng. Government source, not the people's own site; Dhimurru's own site would be a stronger name source.
SWALSC (official) uses Noongar.
Lhere Artepe uses Arrernte / Central Arrernte. Note the official_url body represents the Central Arrernte estate groups of Alice Springs, not all Arrernte.

uluru.gov.au uses Aṉangu. official_url anangu.com.au resolves to APY (Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara), the land body for the APY Lands in South Australia; it does not cover Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa. Acceptable as a representative body, but not one body for all Aṉangu.

Bathurst Regional Council uses Wiradjuri (read via WebFetch; curl gets 403). Council source, not the nation's own; page also lists a Wiradyuri Traditional Owners corporation, a spelling some Wiradjuri bodies use.
State Library of SA uses Kaurna.
Larrakia Nation (official) uses Larrakia; its mission text also spells Larakia.

Spelling Gamilaraay is attested, but name_source_url (ANU course) uses it only as a LANGUAGE name, not as the people's self-name. The NSW native title claim group uses Gomeroi. Recommend a people-level name source (a Gomeroi/Gamilaraay community or native title body) before display.
Nyamba Buru Yawuru (official) uses Yawuru.
Tagai State College page uses Meriam people. Government school source, not the community's own body.
Gunditj Mirring (official) uses Gunditjmara.
Tiwi Land Council uses Tiwi. Its page notes Tiwi consider themselves uniquely Tiwi rather than Aboriginal; display copy should not label them Aboriginal.
Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu uses Ngāi Tahu with macrons.
Official site uses Waikato-Tainui.
Official site uses Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei with macrons.
Te Rūnanga-Ā-Iwi-O-Ngāpuhi site uses Ngāpuhi.
Government page uses Te Arawa and describes it as a large confederation of iwi and hapū; no official_url given.
Settlement page uses Ngāi Tūhoe / Tūhoe; official_url is Tūhoe's own site (Te Uru Taumatua).
Te Rūnanganui o Ngāti Porou uses Ngāti Porou.
Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui uses Whanganui Iwi.
Hokotehi Moriori Trust uses Moriori.
ALK uses Kanak. official_url www.senat-coutumier.nc was unreachable (connection refused) on 2026-10-09; recheck or replace.
Chilean government page uses pueblo Rapa Nui.

Collective descriptor, not one nation's self-name; UNESCO page says 'the people of Papua' and 'communities in Papua and West Papua Provinces'. Consider listing specific peoples. 'West Papuans' in also carries political weight in a contested context; consider dropping it.
TLTB uses iTaukei.
Heiva page uses Ma’ohi in English text and Mā’ohi elsewhere (e.g. Tū’aro Mā’ohi). Name fine; source uses a curly apostrophe.
